edges.notes: CentOS Stream ships Linux kernel packages for supported architectures as part of the distribution.
CentOS Stream on standard ports uses glibc as the C library alongside the dynamic linker.
systemd is the default init and service manager on CentOS Stream releases per project documentation themes.
CentOS Stream services are expressed as systemd unit files and drop-ins on default systemd installs.
CentOS Stream userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC toolchain packages participate in CentOS Stream development and RPM build flows.
GNU binutils participate in standard CentOS Stream RPM build and link flows.
g++-built packages link GNU libstdc++ above glibc on typical CentOS Stream GNU/Linux flows.
Clang/LLVM packages may be installed from CentOS Stream repositories where offered.
Official CentOS Stream OCI images are common glibc-based bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
CRI/containerd nodes run CentOS Stream-based workload images pulled as OCI artifacts.
CentOS Stream is a common node OS choice for clusters seeking RHEL-adjacent glibc userlands.
CentOS Stream bases are packaged as OCI image rootfs layers conforming to OCI image layout conventions.
Substitutable Linux distribution defaults for containers and servers (glibc/systemd vs musl/OpenRC field patterns).
CentOS Stream is documented as the public upstream development branch for RHEL minor-release content.
